Performers
Peabody Symphony Orchestra (orchestra) Documented

Commons and the Archive name the ensemble. The embedded tag ‘Murai/PSO’ is a research lead. Classical Connect separately credits a Peabody performance of this symphony to Hajime Teri Murai, but a link between its recording and these audio files is not established; no full conductor credit or individual players are assigned here.

Work version
Unknown Unknown

Neither source identifies the performing edition. The Peters score used for commentary does not establish which edition was on the players’ desks.

[1] [2]
Recorded
Unknown Unknown

19 November 2006 is the Archive added/public date, repeated by Commons, not a documented performance date. Classical Connect separately lists a Peabody/Murai recording as ‘Recorded on 02/01/2003’, but its identity with these audio files is unconfirmed. The filename code PSO020103 is not decoded as a date.

Processing
The Archive inventory lists 02.PSO020103-Mahler-5-II.mp3 as an original 192 kbps MP3 and its corresponding Ogg Vorbis file as a derivative. Documented

Commons supplies an Ogg Vorbis upload with the embedded encoder Xiph.Org libVorbis I 20040629 and an MP3 access derivative. Its Source link mistakenly selects movement IV within the complete-symphony item. The corresponding movement file is identified from the item inventory and embedded movement title; byte identity and earlier editing or restoration are not established.

[2] [1]
Composition rights
The underlying composition is out of copyright under the ordinary life-plus-70 rule. Inferred, not documented

Mahler died in 1911. This is a term calculation, not worldwide clearance or a statement about an unidentified modern edition.

[4] [5]
Recording rights
Commons applies CC0 1.0 Universal to this recording. Documented

The upstream Archive item links instead to the older Creative Commons public-domain dedication. Neither reviewed record independently establishes the uploader’s authority over the performance. The Commons licence is reported as its rights statement, not independently cleared ownership.

[1] [2]

Gustav Mahler, Symphony No. 5, II. Stürmisch bewegt, mit größter Vehemenz; Peabody Symphony Orchestra. Conductor, session date and venue unestablished. Internet Archive item Mahler_Symphony_5, via Wikimedia Commons; Commons states CC0 1.0 Universal. Rights statement

  1. Wikimedia Commons — Mahler Symphony No. 5, II. Stürmisch bewegt, mit größter Vehemenz.ogg — Summary, Licensing, original-file duration, transcode table and embedded Metadata. The Source URL selects movement IV, although the file title and embedded movement tag identify this movement.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  2. Internet Archive — Mahler Symphony 5 — metadata.creator, licenseurl, addeddate and publicdate; files 02.PSO020103-Mahler-5-II.mp3 and 02.PSO020103-Mahler-5-II.ogg. Item describes complete movements I–V.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  3. Classical Connect — Symphony No. 5, Peabody Symphony Orchestra — Credits Hajime Teri Murai and states ‘Recorded on 02/01/2003, uploaded on 06/07/2010’. Consulted as a candidate provenance lead; the page does not expose an audio filename establishing identity with the selected Commons/Archive files.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  4. Gustav Mahler — biographical dates — Biographical dates: 1860–⁠1911.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  5. Directive 2006/116/EC — copyright term — Articles 1(1) and 8: life plus 70 years, calculated from the following 1 January. No recording-rights calculation is made from this source.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
